links.outcome: Hallucination under Strict RAG, Soft RAG, and LLM-only modes in medical QA and HotpotQA
links.effect: Hallucinated answers remain common even when relevant documents are retrieved. Errors are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that hallucinations in RAG systems are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation, with facet-level analysis exposing systematic evidence override and misalignment patterns that remain hidden under answer-level evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Facet-level diagnostic evaluation of evidence sufficiency and grounding in RAG outputs, using a Facet x Chunk matrix and NLI-based faithfulness scores

screen.practice: retrieval grounding (Strict vs Soft RAG vs LLM-only)
screen.reason: The study evaluates failure modes, hallucination, and evidence grounding across controlled RAG inference modes (strict RAG vs soft RAG vs no retrieval) on medical QA benchmarks.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation grounding modes (strict vs soft RAG)
